title: Energy-efficient SNN Architecture using 3nm FinFET Multiport SRAM-based CIM with Online Learning
problem: Spiking Neural Networks on edge devices face memory-wall bottlenecks that limit throughput and energy efficiency. Traditional single-port SRAM designs restrict memory bandwidth for concurrent operations needed during inference and online learning.
motivation: Edge devices with constrained battery budgets require energy-efficient AI inference accelerators to enable SNN deployment on smartphones, wearables, and IoT systems.
method: This design embeds computation directly into the memory chip, avoiding the energy-wasting delays of shuffling data between separate memory and processors. Multiple read pathways work at the same time, allowing data to be fetched from many locations simultaneously, boosting how much work the system can do per second. The memory ports can read, write, and rearrange data patterns on the fly, letting the hardware update its learning in real-time while still running inference. An arbiter circuit controls traffic between operations and ports, and everything is built using 3nm FinFET transistors—the smallest transistors currently available.
key_novelty: The key innovation is pairing multiple memory pathways with flexible read-write ports that rearrange data, controlled by an arbiter circuit, so the chip can run fast neural network inference and learn from new data simultaneously.
contributions: Multiport SRAM architecture with decoupled read ports achieving 3.1× speedup over single-port designs
Transposable read-write ports enabling online learning directly in the CIM accelerator
Arbiter circuit for efficient port allocation and data processing
System-level demonstration: 44 MInf/s at 607 pJ/Inference and 29mW power
limitations: Abstract does not discuss limitations or design tradeoffs.
primary_theme: Energy-efficient SNN accelerator with multiport SRAM CIM
